rows.summary: A joint Indian air crew and Nepalese army medical team delivered tents, medicines and food to Melamchi on only the third such mission to reach the village after Saturday's 7.8-magnitude earthquake, which killed more than 5,000 people. Nepal's National Emergency Operation Center reported 1,376 deaths in Sindhupalchok District, where Melamchi is located. Local official Upendra Tamang said some 18,000 houses had been destroyed and 100,000 people displaced in the surrounding area. He described conditions as dire and warned that the delivered rice and noodles were nowhere near enough to meet local needs. Tamang said about 500 of the most seriously injured people had already been sent to Kathmandu, mostly by road, but many others remained at the local clinic awaiting help. Seven injured people, five women and two men, were evacuated on the helicopter. Among them was Forshani Tamang, whose family had carried her for four hours to Melamchi and had lost their home and stored grain. Army doctor Naveen Tiwari said the patients mainly had lacerations, their vital signs were stable, and they should recover with antibiotics and intravenous drips. At Kathmandu airbase, paramedics administered IV drips to those who needed them while the relief team prepared for another mission.

At an Anaheim event, J.J. Abrams and the cast unveiled the trailer for "Star Wars: Episode VII -- The Force Awakens," due December 18, to cheering fans. The trailer brought back Han Solo and Chewbacca, while Abrams identified Jakku as an early setting and highlighted actual sets and a BB-8 droid that was not CGI.

Delhi (CNN)An international human rights group is calling for an independent investigation of the killings by police of 20 suspected red sandalwood smugglers in southeastern India. "There must be a criminal investigation to determine whether the police used excessive force, and whether the killings amount to 'fake encounters,' or staged extrajudicial executions", said Abhirr Vp, of Amnesty International India. Amnesty International said the police were claiming self-defense, alleging the suspects attacked them with stone and axes. "However, no police official was injured," the  Amnesty statement said.
